Q: How to get the default for the master branch in Git? A:

This doesn't answer the question itself, but pragmatically the core problem is determining whether a repo uses the main or master naming standard. As such, in most cases we can do this:

git branch | grep -m1 -Eow "master|main"
  • -E — extended regexp (because of the |)
  • -o — print only the match
  • -w — match whole words
  • -m1 — print only the first match

Q: .NET's CLR in WebAssembly A:

suggests that its virtual machine still shouldn't be able to efficiently represent the CLR properly

Correct. That is why Blazor first deploys a compiled-to-WASM version of Mono.
Blazor brings its own CLR to the party.

Your application code won't be compiled to Wasm, it will be deployed as (regular) IL that is executed by Mono. With the dev tools you can see a bunch of .DLL files being downloaded to your browser. You can in principle use any .net standard package that fits within the Browser security sandbox.

What exactly does WebAssembly bring to the table that wasn't possible with JavaScript alone?

It enables a C compiler to compile Mono.*.c to Mono.wasm.
And it is fast.

Q: Specify argument and return types of dict transpose function A:

To define a transposable dictionary type and its transposition type, please use TypeVar from the typing module. Please try the below code:

from collections import defaultdict
from typing import TypeVar, Dict, Set

# Define type variables for the keys and values
K = TypeVar('K')
V = TypeVar('V')

def transpose_dict(dct: Dict[K, Set[V]]) -> Dict[V, Set[K]]:
    transposed = defaultdict(set)

    for key, value_set in dct.items():
        for inv_key in value_set:
            transposed[inv_key].add(key)
            
    return transposed
